introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Logic (0590), Paper 2, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B. ONLY THE FIRST FIVE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

All the questions carry 20 marks. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

In solving, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
incertitudes: Q5(c)(ii) : « ~ (p v q) . q » est lu comme (~(p v q)) . q, la négation ne portant que sur la parenthèse : valeur Faux. Si l'on lisait ~[(p v q) . q], le résultat serait Vrai ; la lecture usuelle est celle retenue.

Q5(d)(i) : la converse d'une proposition A est la converse par limitation (« Some teachers are examiners ») ; la conversion simple « All teachers are examiners » est illicite. Le jury peut avoir accepté l'une ou l'autre.
Q5(d)(ii) : la ligne « All musicians are dancers. » est imprimée deux fois avant le syllogisme (ligne parasite) ; recopiée telle quelle dans l'énoncé.
Q5(e)(ii) : sophisme retenu : argument d'ignorance (ad ignorantiam).

Règle de choix : la page de garde dit « answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B ; only the first five questions answered will be marked ». Section A (questions 1 à 3) : toutes obligatoires, donc aucune règle ; Section B (questions 4 à 6) : `parmi 2 sur 3`. La règle « les cinq premières réponses seules sont corrigées » est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.
Points : chaque question est imprimée « 20 marks ». Chaque sous-question (a) à (e) vaut 4 points (2 x 2) ; Q2(a) est imprimée « 4x1 marks ». 5 x 4 = 20 : aucun écart de somme.

Aucun corrigé officiel ; les corrigés sont des réponses modèles de manuel de logique traditionnelle (définitions, règles de distribution, carré des oppositions avec import existentiel). Les tables de vérité, la validité du dilemme constructif complexe et des syllogismes (AEE-2, AAA-1, EAE-1) sont recalculées avec Python. À faire relire par un enseignant de logique : les définitions varient d'un manuel à l'autre.

Sujet scanné de 8 pages avec filigrane gcerevision.com / KAWLO, sans incidence sur la lecture ; aucune figure. Page de garde vérifiée : ORDINARY LEVEL, Logic, code 0590, Paper 2, JUNE 2025, deux heures et demie.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Classify these Terms under Universal Terms or Particular Terms: "Few students; all intellectuals; some girls; every child".

(ii) Criticise the following Definition: "Happiness is the absence of sadness". (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **Universal terms:** "all intellectuals", "every child" (they refer to every member of the class). **Particular terms:** "few students", "some girls" (they refer to only part of the class).

**(ii)** The definition is faulty:
- It is **negative**: it says what happiness is not, not what it is, although a definition should be affirmative when it can be.
- It is **too wide**: a person in deep sleep or a stone has no sadness but is not happy, so the definiens applies to more than the definiendum.
- It defines a term by its **contrary** (sadness), which itself has to be understood through happiness.
themes: O Level Logic - definition and division

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Using the Disjuncts, "Tom is a police officer"; "John is a teacher", construct a Disjunctive Proposition.

(ii) Express the following Proposition into Standard Form: "Not all Principals are corrupt persons". (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **"Either Tom is a police officer or John is a teacher."**

**(ii)** "Not all Principals are corrupt persons" denies the universal A proposition "All Principals are corrupt persons", so it is its contradictory, the O proposition: **"Some Principals are not corrupt persons."**
themes: O Level Logic - propositions and their types

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Symbolise the statement "Joe is neither in class nor in his office" using the variables p and q.

(ii) Given the variables; "p" and "q" as False, determine the Truth-Value of $\sim (p \vee q) \cdot q$. (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Let p = "Joe is in class" and q = "Joe is in his office". "Neither p nor q" means not p and not q: **$\sim p \cdot \sim q$**, equivalent to $\sim (p \vee q)$.

**(ii)** With p = F and q = F:
- $p \vee q$ = F
- $\sim (p \vee q)$ = T
- $\sim (p \vee q) \cdot q$ = T . F = **False**.

(The negation sign applies only to the bracket $(p \vee q)$, and the dot is the main connective.)
themes: O Level Logic - symbolic logic basics

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Give the Converse of " All examiners are teachers".

(ii) Identify and write out the Minor and Major Terms of the Categorical Syllogism below:

"All musicians are dancers.

"All musicians are dancers

All artists are musicians.

Therefore, all artists are dancers". (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** "All examiners are teachers" is an A proposition. An A proposition cannot be converted simply ("All teachers are examiners" would be an illicit conversion). It is converted by limitation (per accidens): the terms are exchanged and the quantity is reduced. **Converse: "Some teachers are examiners."**

**(ii)** Conclusion: "All artists are dancers".
- **Minor term** (subject of the conclusion): **artists**.
- **Major term** (predicate of the conclusion): **dancers**.
- (Middle term: musicians.)

The form is A A A in the first figure (Barbara), a valid syllogism.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) (i) Complete this Argument by providing the Minor Premise and Conclusion to make a Modus Ponens:

"If the message of righteousness is preached, then people will repent"

(ii) Examine the Argument below and indicate the Fallacy most clearly committed in it:

"Since nobody has died and come back to prove it, the claim of immortality must be unacceptable." (2x2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** In a Modus Ponens the minor premise affirms the antecedent and the conclusion affirms the consequent:

- If the message of righteousness is preached, then people will repent.
- **The message of righteousness is preached.**
- **Therefore, people will repent.**

**(ii)** **Argument from ignorance (argumentum ad ignorantiam).** The claim of immortality is rejected only because it has not been proved true; lack of proof is wrongly taken as proof that the claim is false. It is a fallacy of relevance.
